name: Gmail

steps.d: In the Google Cloud console, go to IAM & Admin → Create a project and give it a name.
In APIs & Services → Library, open the Gmail API and click Enable.
Fill in Branding, choose a user type under Audience, and add yourself as a test user.
Pick the narrowest scopes you need, such as gmail.labels or gmail.send. Reading mail needs a restricted scope like gmail.readonly.
Google Auth Platform → Clients → Create client. Add your HTTPS redirect URIs, then save the client secret: it's shown only once.

steps.t: Submit for verification (only to go public)
steps.d: Needed for sensitive and restricted Gmail scopes. Restricted scopes also need a security assessment if you store the data on servers.

blockers.s: In Testing, only up to 100 listed test users can sign in, and their authorizations expire after seven days.
Scopes that read mail, such as gmail.readonly and gmail.modify, are restricted and may need a security assessment.
Authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console.

sources: Configure the OAuth consent screen and choose scopes
diffReason: Hard: you can test right away, but Gmail's sensitive and restricted scopes must complete Google's verification before you go public, and restricted scopes may need a security assessment

checklist.answer: In the Google Cloud console, open Google Auth Platform, go to Clients and click Create client. You first have to register the app under Branding.
Client types are Web application, Android, iOS, Chrome Extension, TVs and Limited-input devices, and Desktop app.
Branding asks for an app name, a user support email, an app home page, privacy policy and terms of service links, authorized domains and developer contact information.
Redirect URIs must use HTTPS, except localhost. They can't contain wildcards or fragments.
You get a client ID and a client secret. The secret is shown only once, when you create the client, so store it securely.
gmail.labels is non-sensitive and gmail.send is sensitive. Reading mail with gmail.readonly or gmail.modify, or full access with mail.google.com, is restricted.

Sensitive scopes need additional OAuth app verification, and restricted scopes need restricted scope verification. If you store restricted scope data on servers, you must also go through a security assessment.
Google's estimates are 2-3 business days for brand verification, 10 business days for sensitive scopes and 6 weeks for restricted scopes. They aren't guaranteed.
In Testing status, only up to 100 listed test users can sign in, and their authorizations expire after seven days.
A verification request can be rejected if your scope justification is judged insufficient, or if the app home page isn't hosted on a domain you've verified.
